title: Missing Numbers on a Number Line Worksheets for Kindergarten
intro: Help your student use the labels already shown on a number line.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Read the first label and count each equal interval forward by one. Pause at the missing label and check against the next printed number.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Read the visible starting number first: point to 3 and say “three.” Move to the next mark and say “four.” One more step reaches the empty box: “five.” Continue with the printed 6 and 7 to check.

The missing number is 5. It is one more than four and one less than six. Counting forward and checking the next visible label lead to the same answer.

Point to every card that is greater than 1 and less than 4. More than one card may work.

1234

Let the child check each card against both parts of the question. Use counters if needed: does its group have more than one counter, and fewer than four?

Show all the matching cards and explain why

The matching cards are 2 and 3. Saying 3 and 2 identifies the same cards and is also correct.

1234

Two and three are each greater than one and less than four. One is not greater than itself. Four is not less than itself. The two end cards therefore do not match the question.

If Ben chooses only 2, he has found one correct card. Ask, “Does another card also pass both checks?” If he includes 4, compare a group of four counters with another group of four: they are equal, so neither has fewer counters.

Ask your student

Does our number fit between its two neighbors?

If your student needs help

If the student counts tick marks from one, point back to the actual starting label.
